newsitem.title: GERMANY: Greenpeace in soymeal protest at German feed plant.
newsitem.headline: Greenpeace in soymeal protest at German feed plant.

text.p: The environmental group Greenpeace on Tuesday targeted a German compound feed plant in a continuing protest over the use of transgenic soymeal.
A Greenpeace spokesman at the site of the protest in the North-Rhine Westphalian town of Muenster said 12 activists had climbed on the roof of Raiffeisen-Central-Genossenschaft.
He said the plant was using meal derived from imported United States soybeans genetically modified by Monsanto Co .
"We intend to stay there overnight or longer to show our protest at the use of genetically modified soybean meal in animal feeds," he said.
"At least, it should be used separately from the conventional soybean product and labelled accordingly so that farmers would have a choice in what they are buying."
Plant management had approached the activists and defended the use of transgenic soymeal, the Greenpeace spokesman said.
The protest is the third of its kind after Greenpeace targeted two feeds plants belonging to the Raiffeisen group in Bavaria and Schleswig-Holstein state last month.
Deutsche Raiffeisenverband (DRV) is the umbrella organisation of German farm co-ops.
The spokesman said the protest was also aimed at maintaining pressure on the Brussels authorities to enhance labelling stipulations on so-called novel foods.

New EU regulations on such foods came into effect this month, which Greenpeace says have too many loopholes. Greenpeace also wants to prevent the cultivation of transgenic food crops on European soil.
